relevance.rationale: Groebner-Shirshov bases for Coxeter GROUPS W = sgp<Sigma | (s s')^m = 1>. None of the folio's live fronts (Hecke -> TL Wedderburn weights, meander/Gram determinant, Connes spectral distance, Young-lattice corners, NN binding, Kashaev spine) appears in it. It is supporting rather than tangential because it lands on a named, live piece of folio machinery: the Groebner-Shirshov warrant for H_n(q). Two things it supplies. (1) Example 3.2 (pp. 4-5) refutes by explicit counterexample the Bokut-Shiao conjecture that a GS basis of an arbitrary Coxeter group is obtainable from S = {(1),(2),(3')} using only the commuting relations, and its introduction restricts the known positive results to FINITE Coxeter groups; type A_{n-1} is finite, so the folio's own case is untouched, and recording that is the point so nobody later invokes 'GS bases for Coxeter groups' generically. (2) Its bibliography, entry [4] on p. 21, supplies the coordinates for the refid [bokut2001], which was cited at QOU/Archimedean/MassGapGm.lean:46 and named in the References block of UGB/GrobnerShirshov/HeckeGS.lean with no entry in references.ts; that entry was created in the same commit as this row, from three agreeing bibliographies in this batch. WRITER CORRECTION to the triage that produced this row: it described a live axiom hecke_is_gs_basis at HeckeGS.lean:153-158, justified in an axiom-budget table as 'Bokut & Shiao 2001, Thm 3.5' and carrying an inline '-- Ref: [bokutchen2014]'. On this branch that axiom does NOT exist. It was deleted as FALSE, and NotAGSBasis.hecke_not_gs_basis_four machine-refutes it at n = 4; the module header says so and names the missing Bokut-Shiao completion family sigma_i sigma_{i-1} ... sigma_j sigma_i -> sigma_{i-1} sigma_i sigma_{i-1} ... sigma_j. The document's value survives the correction and sharpens: the live consumer is bean qou-auq3 (complete the system), and the scope note belongs there. What this document does NOT do, and why it is not core: it proves nothing about H_n(q), never mentions a deformation parameter, and so cannot license the transfer from C[W] to the Hecke algebra that qou-auq3 needs. Scope-(a) negative: as read, it supplies no lemma that closes a gap in the folio's own argument; its value is scoping and bibliographic hygiene.

keyResults.statement: For Sigma = {s1<s2<s3<s4} with m12 = m23 = m24 = infinity, m13 = 3, m14 = 2, m34 = 5, the set S = {(1),(2),(3')} is NOT a Groebner-Shirshov basis of W; the corrected basis (1) u (2) u (3'') is exhibited.
keyResults.useForFolio: Fixes the scope of the folio's Groebner-Shirshov warrant: there is no general-Coxeter theorem to appeal to, only a finite-type one. Type A_{n-1} is finite so nothing the folio asserts is affected, but bean qou-auq3 must cite the finite-type result and not a general claim.

keyResults.statement: S = {(1),(2),(3')} is a Groebner-Shirshov basis of W whenever no f in (3') has any of the four inclusion-composition properties C1-C4; three explicit families of Coxeter matrices satisfy this, including (i) all m_ij >= 3 for i > j.
keyResults.useForFolio: Unconditional, non-finiteness-based warrant for the q=1 shadow of the smallest case: the rank-2 matrix m12 = 3 (W = S_3, whose six elements index the normal forms of def:hecke-normal-form) satisfies (i). For n >= 4 none of the three families applies (m_13 = 2 kills (i) and (ii), m_21 = 3 kills (iii)), so there the warrant reverts to the finite-type theorem. Either way this is W, not H_n(q), and any remark must say so.

proposedActions.rationale: Record in the HeckeGS.lean module header and in qou-auq3 that (a) there is no general-Coxeter GS theorem -- Example 3.2 refutes the conjecture and the positive results are finite-type, which does cover type A_{n-1} -- and (b) this document, like the Bokut-Shiao paper it follows, treats the Coxeter GROUP and never H_n(q), so the transfer to the deformation is an open point qou-auq3 must not assume. Deliberately NOT aid-proof: nothing here discharges anything.

The q-deformed type-A statement that qou-auq3 actually needs is not in this document and not in [bokut2001]; two other documents in this batch attribute it to Kang-Lee-Lee-Oh, J. Algebra 252 (2002) 258-292 §6. Obtain and triage that paper before citing it as load-bearing.
